findings.title: Downstream TDD impact not separately enumerated
findings.detail: C3 asks that downstream impact on SPEC AND TDD be enumerated. SPEC impact is well-enumerated (§3 'SPEC-01 inherits this contract', §6 downstream_refs name SPEC-01 interface/data-model/write-ordering, §9 downstream mapping). The TDD layer is only seeded implicitly via the §8 verification table and §8 BDD cross-references; there is no explicit statement of what the downstream TDD must prove (durability-at-ack crash probe, unique-constraint property test, fail-closed deny-on-grant-unavailable test, synchronous_commit config-drift assertion). The §8 verification table is an adequate test surface, so this is a clarity gap rather than a missing primitive.
findings.recommendation: Add one line in §9 (Downstream) naming the TDD obligations this ADR seeds so the Test Architect inherits an explicit test surface rather than inferring it from §8.

findings.title: Sibling cross-references use BRD-topic refs as proxies for not-yet-authored ADR IDs (carried from iter 1; acceptable)
findings.detail: The §10 relationship table references siblings by BRD origin (BRD.01.08.66e2, .5b91, .c478, .9665, .daeb) rather than @adr:/@depends: form, because those sibling ADRs are not yet authored. The note 'Depends-on cross-links resolve once those siblings are authored' and the Appendix @depends: future-form note make the deferred linkage explicit, so the form is acceptable for forward references to unauthored siblings. Residual risk is drift: when siblings are authored these BRD proxies must be replaced with @adr:/@depends: references, and nothing pins that obligation to a specific cross-ADR ID. Retained as P3 from iteration 1 since it remains a deferred-linkage note, not a defect to block on now.
findings.recommendation: When the sibling ADRs land, replace each BRD proxy in §10 with the concrete @depends:/@adr: reference (e.g., the cache topic becomes @depends: ADR-NN), keeping BRD origin as the secondary anchor. No change required at this iteration.

findings.title: Re-scoped §8 p95 criterion resolves the prior implementability concern; no-cache envelope budget left to SPEC/TDD
findings.detail: Verifying the prior-iteration P2 (TL-ADR-01-001): §8 now reads 'PK read path within budget under the no-cache MVP load envelope (p95 < 50 ms jointly owned with BRD.01.08.66e2, verifiable once the cache lands)'. This re-scopes the in-ADR commitment to PK-read-within-envelope and explicitly defers the binding p95 < 50 ms to the cache topic, so the ADR no longer binds itself to a criterion unverifiable within its own no-cache decided scope. The C1/hidden-coupling implementability concern from iteration 1 is RESOLVED. Residual (P3): the 'no-cache MVP load envelope' budget the PK read must hit is not given a number here; acceptable at ADR altitude (a numeric PK-read budget is a SPEC/TDD concern), worth only a pointer so the downstream test author knows that envelope target is theirs to fix.
findings.recommendation: Optionally add a parenthetical in the §8 row noting the no-cache PK-read budget value is set at SPEC/TDD (downstream), distinct from the cache-gated p95 < 50 ms jointly owned with BRD.01.08.66e2. The re-scope as written already clears the implementability bar; no P1/P2 remains.
